On 23 April 2022, an unreported number of people, including students, marched as part of 'Walk a Mile in Their Her His Our Shoes' in Greensburg (Pennsylvania) to call for an end to and raise awareness of gender-based violence.

On 23 April 2022, an unreported number of people convoyed through Philadelphia and Reading before they demonstrated in front of the Capitol Building in Harrisburg (Pennsylvania) in opposition to coronavirus policies and vaccine mandates. Most of the rally participants were members of 'The People's Convoy', an anti-coronavirus vaccine mandate freedom convoy. At least one of the cars participating had 'Let's Go Brandon' written on it.

On 22 April 2022, an unreported number of people marched from Paoli, Pennsylvania to Vanground Group's headquarters in Malvern (Pennsylvania) to call on the firm to stop investing in fossil fuels. The march was attended by members of Earth Quaker Action Team, Chester Residents Concerned for Quality Living, Exodus Alliance, Extinction Rebellion, Sierra Club, Third Act, Elders Action Network, Interfaith Power and Light, 350 (an international climate action organization), Dayenu (a Jewish climate action organization), and Eastwick Friends and Neighbors Coalition as well as students as part of the 'Fight for Our Future' rallies held nationwide to commemorate Earth Day.

On 22 April 2022, an unreported number of people rallied in Love Park in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call for the reformation of the Department of Human Services. The rally came in the wake of a report released by the Philadelphia City Council Special Committee On Child Separation which concluded that the Department often 'needlessly' placed children into foster care. A Christian Bishop, Philadelphia Sheriff Rochelle Bilal (D), City Councilmember David Oh (R), and City Councilmember Cindy Bass (D) attended the rally.

On 22 April 2022, a small group of protesters held a 'Fight For Our Future' march in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for better public transit services to help combat climate change. This protest was organized by Pittsburghers for Public Transit and attended by the local ATU president. Shortly after, an unreported number of people demonstrated at the City County Building to call for action to address climate change and environmental inequality. This protest was organized by the Green Party, Pittsburghers for Public Transit, and Sunrise Movement. Both protests were held in commemoration of Earth Day and later merged.

Non-violent activity: On 22 April 2022, antisemitic flyers were found in Ardmore (Pennsylvania) associating Jewish people with Disney, which they referred to as 'child groomers,' and promoting the Goyim Defense League. The reference to 'groomers' comes after Disney said it opposes Florida's 'don't say gay' legislation.

On 21 April 2022, roughly 60 people demonstrated outside of City Hall in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call for increased funding for the city's parks and recreation programs in the mayor's budget. The rally was organized by Philadelphia Parks Alliance as part of the Rec It Philly campaign and was attended by Councilmembers Jamie Gauthier (D) and Cherelle Parker (D).

On 21 April 2022, an unreported number of students camped on the College Green at the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call on the University to divest from fossil fuels and increase its support for environmental justice efforts. The protest was organized by Fossil Free Penn and visited by the Maldivian Ambassador to the United States, Thilmeeza Hussain.

On 21 April 2022, a small group of people gathered for a pro-Ukraine and anti-Russia rally near the Russian flag on the Benjamin Franklin Parkway in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the Russian invasion of Ukraine and to call for the Russian flag on the Parkway to be taken down. The protest was attended by at least one member of the Ukrainian community.

On 21 April 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for 'fair wages' and 'accountability' for workers at PPG. The protest was organized by IUPAT (which is part of the AFL-CIO) and attended by State Representative Nick Pisciottano (D) and members of the AFGE.

On 20 April 2022, at least 6 students camped on the College Green at the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call on the University to divest from fossil fuels and increase its support for environmental justice efforts. The protest was organized by Fossil Free Penn.

On 20 April 2022, an unreported number of people rallied outside of the City-County Building in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for police accountability in the death of a Black man after he was tasered by eight police officers in October 2021 as well as accountability for the 'assault' of a protestor by an officer at a protest on 16 April 2022. The rally was led by the group Justice for Jim Rogers.

On 19 April 2022, about 20 students camped on the College Green at the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call on the University to divest from fossil fuels and increase its support for environmental justice efforts. University police asked the students to leave after which only 6 remained to camp through the night. The protest was organized by Fossil Free Penn.

On 19 April 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of Sen. Pat Toomey's office in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the Senator and to call for action against climate change, such as a reduction in emissions which harm human health. Members of ReImagine Appalachia and Moms Clean Air Force participated in the protest which was organized by Tuesdays with Toomey.

On 18 April 2022, an unreported number of people gathered for a vigil in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to condemn gun violence and show solidarity with those impacted by the death of a 7-year-old boy who died after being shot by an unknown assailant.

On 18 April 2022, approximately 15 demonstrators interrupted a forum in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call on the University of Pennsylvania to prevent the eviction of residents of the University City Townhomes and for the president of the University to meet with the residents. The protest was organized by the Save the UC Townhomes Coalition (which is made up of Penn faculty, students, community members, and a Black group known as the Black Bottom Tribe) and was mostly attended by students.

On 16 April 2022, roughly 20 protesters demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for police accountability in the death of a Black man after he was tasered by eight police officers in October 2021. The protesters were blocking the road when police declared the protest an unlawful assembly and attempted to disperse the protest. When the protesters did not leave, the police attempted to arrest a protester, but another protester stepped between the two and pushed the officer away. The officer then punched the intervening protester in the face. The two protesters were subsequently arrested.

On 15 April 2022, community members marched from Homewood to East Liberty in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for peace and an end to gun violence in the community. Members of the House of Manna church, the Black Political Empowerment Project, and the Neighborhood Resilience Project participated.
On 14 April 2022, students held a 'Take Back The Night' rally and march at Penn State University in State College (Pennsylvania) to show support for survivors of sexual violence.

On 14 April 2022, students held a 'Take Back The Night' rally and march at East Stroudsburg University in East Stroudsburg (Pennsylvania) to show support for survivors of sexual violence. Women's Resources of Monroe County organized the event.

On 14 April 2022, a group of students held a 'die-in' rally at City Hall in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to demand action and resources to address gun violence. March for Our Lives Philadelphia organized the rally, and the Charles Foundation participated.

On 13 April 2022, dozens of students protested at the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to demand justice and call for support for a former student who had her sexual assault claim questioned by the university, who claimed the student had 'misrepresented' her self-report.

On 13 April 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated at the Capitol in Harrisburg (Pennsylvania) to call for 'equitable' funding for education in the state. State Sen. Nikil Saval (D) and members of CASA participated in the rally which was organized by State Sen. Vincent Hughes (D).

On 12 April 2022, a group of people rallied in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to demand an end to gun violence and to call for justice in the case of a 15 year old boy who was fatally shot in Wissinoming on 24 March.

On 12 April 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of Sen. Pat Toomey's office in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the Senator. One protester held a sign in support of Ukraine amidst the Russian invasion. The protest was organized by Tuesdays with Toomey.

On 11 April 2022, an unreported number of people rallied in the State Capitol Building in Harrisburg (Pennsylvania) to call for a permanent fund to assist renters in the state. The rally was held by Make the Road PA, a Latinx organization, alongside State Senator Nikil Saval (D) and State Representatives Sara Innamorato (D) and Elizabeth Fielder (D).

On 8 April 2022, an unreported number of students staged a walkout and rally at Bodine High School in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in protest of conditions at the school, such as frequent fights and insensitivity toward members of the LGBTQ+ community.

On 7 April 2022, an unreported number of people gathered in Philadelphia City Hall in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call for the reopening of the school budget and for funding for specific 'critical' positions in schools. Philadelphia City Councilmembers Helen Gym (D), Kendra Brooks (WFP), Derek Green (D), and Mark Squilla (D) spoke at the rally which was organized by the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers, Teamsters, POWER (an interfaith organization), and Our City Our Schools.

On 7 April 2022, an unreported number of people, mostly students, marched in the 'Penn State Men Against Violence Walk' on the Pennsylvania State University campus in State College (Pennsylvania) in opposition to sexual violence on the campus and to show support for survivors. The event was organized by the Penn State Gender Equity Center and the Interfraternity Council in collaboration with other organizations. Later in the evening, an unreported number of people marched in a 'Take Back the Night' walk in opposition to sexual and domestic violence in the campus community. This event was organized by the Lambda Theta Alpha sorority.

On 6 April 2022, four dozen people rallied outside of The Meadows Psychiatric Center in Centre Hall (Pennsylvania) in support of unionization efforts at the facility. The rally was attended by members of the SEIU, health workers, State Representative Scott Conklin (D), College Township Councilmember Paul Takac (D), and Centre County Controller Jason Moser.

On 6 April 2022, an unreported number of people rallied in York (Pennsylvania) to call on Congress to pass legislation investing in climate change solutions. Rep. Carol Hill-Evans (D), York Mayor Michael Helfrich (D), a Venezuelan migrant, and members of CASA and Climate Action Campaign participated in the rally.

On 5 April 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of Sen. Pat Toomey's office in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the Senator. Protesters held signs in support of Ukraine amidst the Russian invasion and to call for the USPS to be fixed. The protest was organized by Tuesdays with Toomey.

On 3 April 2022, about 50 people marched around Payrow Plaza in Bethlehem (Pennsylvania) as part of the 'March for Peace and Unity' in opposition to 'white supremacist hate speech.' The event was attended by Pennsylvania State Representative Steve Samuelson (D), Bethlehem Mayor J. William Reynolds (D), Bethlehem City Council people Grace Smith and Dr. Wandalyn Enix, and a rabbi, as well as members of the Pennsylvania Human Relations Committee, Lehigh-Pocono Committee of Concern, and the Bethlehem NAACP.

On 3 April 2022, about 100 people demonstrated as part of the 'March Against Sexual Violence' in the Oakland neighborhood of Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to speak out against sexual violence and to show support to survivors. The march was organized in part by Project SAFE alongside Carlow, the University of Pittsburgh, Carnegie Mellon University, and other community organizations and was attended by students and members of Underdog, an advocacy organization for victims of sexual violence.

On 2 April 2022, more than 100 people rallied in Chambersburg Square in Chambersburg (Pennsylvania) to call for the nondiscrimination ordinance in the city to be reinstated as well as to show support for the transgender community around the International Transgender Day of Visibility. The event was attended by members of PA Coalition for Trans Youth and Lititz Chooses Love as well as several Christian pastors and Chambersburg Councilmember Alice Elia (D).

On 2 April 2022, a large crowd of people, mostly students, rallied in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for an end to gun violence. The event was held in response to a shooting of a young teenage boy on 30 March 2022, who was shot while riding his bike during the day in the neighborhood.

On 1 April 2022, hundreds of people rallied outside of the Philadelphia Museum of Art in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in support of unionized workers at the museum as they seek a union contract. The event was attended by members of the AFSCME, UFCW, AFL-CIO, DSA, Socialist Alternative, CPUSA, and the Philadelphia Young Communist League as well as State Senators Sharif Street (D) and Nikil Saval (D).

On 31 March 2022, an unreported number of people gathered outside of City Hall in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the mayor's proposed budget for 2023. The rally was attended by members of Act Up Philadelphia, Amistad Law Project, AFSCME, Alliance for a Just Philadelphia, and Philly Neighborhood Networks as well as a Christian pastor.

On 31 March 2022, nearly 60 people gathered in front of the City-County Building in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) in opposition to legislation being passed nationwide which they claim is anti-trans and to celebrate International Transgender Day of Visibility. The Pittsburgh Mayor's Press Secretary Maria Montano spoke at the rally which was held by Trans YOUniting, True T PGH, Proud Haven, SWOP Pittsburgh, The Love Diamond Project, and TransPride Pittsburgh.

On 30 March 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated at Philadelphia International Airport (Pennsylvania) to call for 'good' union contracts for airport workers. On 29 March 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of Sen. Pat Toomey's office in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the Senator. The protest was organized by Tuesdays with Toomey.

On 28 March 2022, roughly 100 people demonstrated in Harrisburg (Pennsylvania) to call on state lawmakers to address food insecurity among college students. On 28 March 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of City Hall in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call for more funding for libraries in the upcoming city budget. City Councilmembers Helen Gym (D), Kendra Brooks (WFP), and Jamie Gauthier (D) spoke at the event.

On 28 March 2022, over 100 people demonstrated as part of the 'Medical Freedom Rally' at the Capitol in Harrisburg (Pennsylvania) to call for 'broken trust and greed in medicine' to be fixed. Members of the anti-coronavirus vaccine mandate freedom convoy, 'The People's Convoy', also attended the event. On 28 March 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call for justice in the shooting death of a 12-year-old boy by plainclothes police officers on 1 March 2022.

City Councilmember Helen Gym (D) spoke at the rally which was held by Teamsters Local 502 and the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers (an AFT affiliate).

On 24 March 2022, 10 people demonstrated outside of the Dormont municipal building in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for justice in the death of a Black man who died in police custody after repeatedly being tased and denied medical attention when he asked as well as to show support for witnesses testifying before a grand jury in the man's death. The rally was held by the group 'Justice for Jim Rogers'.

On 24 March 2022, about 70 people rallied on the Pennsylvania State University campus in State College (Pennsylvania) to show support for a professor who faced several charges after a physical altercation with a counter-protester at a coronavirus vaccine mandate protest as well as to protest the school administration's termination proceedings against the professor. The event was held by Penn State Students Against Sexist Violence.

On 23 March 2022, an unreported number of people rallied at Duquesne University in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for a fair contract for dining workers unionized with the SEIU. City Councilpersons Deb Gross (D), Bobby Wilson (D), Corey O'Conner (D), and Dewitt Walton (D) attended the rally.

On 22 March 2022, an unreported number of people, including students, demonstrated outside of the Elizabethtown Area School District school board meeting in Elizabethtown (Pennsylvania) in opposition to proposed spending cuts in the school district.

On 22 March 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of Sen. Pat Toomey's office in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the Senator as well as to call on the media to change the ways in which it reports on gun violence. There was at least one sign calling for 'sane gun laws.' Members of the Philadelphia Center for Gun Violence and CeaseFire PA participated in the protest which was organized by Tuesdays with Toomey.

On 22 March 2022, an unreported number of Port Authority employees demonstrated outside of the Allegheny County Courthouse in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the Port Authority's coronavirus vaccine mandate for employees.

On 20 March 2022, dozens of people gathered for a pro-Ukraine and anti-Russia rally in Wilkes-Barre (Pennsylvania) to show support for Ukraine amidst the Russian invasion and to call on the American government to close the airspace above Ukraine. On 19 March 2022, dozens of people, including students, gathered for the 'Complacency Kills' march and rally at the Allen Street Gates in State College (Pennsylvania) to call for justice in the death of a Black man who was killed by State College police officers while experiencing a mental health crisis. On 18 March 2022, dozens of people, including Port Authority of Allegheny County workers, demonstrated outside of the Port Authority building in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the agency's coronavirus vaccination mandate and their denial of religious exemptions to some workers.

On 15 March 2022, around 75 people rallied outside of the Behavioral Health and Intellectual disAbility Services headquarters in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call for the city to implement non-police mobile crisis responses for mental health emergencies. On 15 March 2022, an unreported number of people, including students, rallied in Lansdowne (Pennsylvania) to call for equitable education funding in the state. On 15 March 2022, more than 50 students, teachers and other staff and supporters demonstrated outside of the Eisenhower Science and Technology Leadership Academy in Norristown (Pennsylvania) to call for equitable education and fair school funding in the state. The Greater Norristown NAACP Education Chairman, Education Law Center Legal Director, Norristown Area School District Board President Phil Daniels (D), Superintendent Christopher Dormer, and School Board Vice President Monica D'Antonio (D) spoke at the event. The event was organized by Children First and Education Voters of Pennsylvania. This event was part of fair funding vigils held throughout the state on the same day.

On 15 March 2022, more than 60 people rallied outside of Pottstown Middle School in Pottstown (Pennsylvania) to call for equitable education and fair school funding in the state. A Protestant Christian Reverend, policy advisor from the Education Law Center, Vice President of the Federation of Pottstown Teachers, Pottstown School Board members Laura Johnson and Mark Ellison III, and Superintendent Stephen Rodriguez all spoke at the event which was also attended by students, parents, and other community members. On 11 March 2022, about 60 people, mostly students, gathered for a rally and march in Market Square in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) in opposition to bills that have been passed in various states nationwide which restricts the freedom of LGBTQ+ people to exist in the public sphere as well as to show support for LGBTQ+ people affected by the laws.

Other: On 1 March 2022, a 12-year-old boy was shot and killed by plainclothes police officers in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania). According to police, four plainclothes officers were sitting in an unmarked vehicle in a neighborhood after receiving reports that a teenager and a young adult were in the area with weapons. The officers approached the 12-year-old boy and his teenage friend, who were both riding bikes. The officers gave conflicting reasons for why they wanted to stop the boys. After turning on their flashing lights, a bullet pierced the car's back window. Two of the officers left the car, then chased the young boy and his friend before shooting the 12-year-old in the back and killing him. An investigation into the shooting found that, after pursuing the boys, police fired three shots, and one of the officers fired the fatal shot at the boy from near-point blank range while the boy was facedown on the ground and knowingly unarmed. The boy had tossed his gun while being chased by officers, and was reported to have been attempting to surrender. The officer responsible for killing the boy was fired and was charged with murder in May 2022.
